previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for a planned coil embolization of the renal artery to manage complications from a failed kidney transplant. Due to prior abdominal wall reconstruction, surgical removal was deemed high-risk, so a minimally invasive approach was chosen. The procedure was performed successfully without complications. Post-procedure, she remained on bedrest, ambulated without difficulty, and tolerated a regular diet. The transplant team recommended discontinuing Myfortic and initiating a short steroid taper, while continuing tacrolimus. She completed a scheduled hemodialysis session and had stable vital signs. Her warfarin was planned for restart post-discharge with INR monitoring. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions for incision care, activity, and follow-up with her nephrologist.
problems: Surgical operation with transplant of whole organ causing abnormal patient reaction, or later complication, without mention of misadventure at time of operation

radiology_notes.text:
CLINICAL INFORMATION:  ___ female with right lower quadrant renal
transplant for polycystic kidney, recently underwent coil embolization of the
transplant kidney due to chronic rejection.

TECHNIQUE:  Transabdominal sonographic images were obtained.

___.

FINDINGS:  The transplant kidney parenchyma is diffusely hypoechoic, with
echogenic scattered foci seen throughout, some of which exhibit ring-down
artifact.  The main renal vein appears completely thrombosed.  Shadowing
material in the region of the renal hilum likely represents embolic material. 
On color Doppler imaging, some flow is seen, without a normal arterial
waveform, likely largely venous.  There is no perinephric collection.

IMPRESSION:  Transplant kidney, with scattered echogenic foci, raising concern
for small locules of gas, without normal arterial waveforms consistent with
history of coil embolization.  On color Doppler imaging, some flow is seen,
without a normal arterial waveform, likely largely venous
